old_caption: The video captures a nighttime urban scene, likely taken from a stationary position on a wet road. The reflections of streetlights and vehicle headlights create a shimmering effect on the wet pavement, enhancing the sense of a rainy night. Several vehicles are visible, their headlights and taillights streaking across the frame due to the long exposure time used for the shot. The lights from these vehicles form elongated trails, adding a dynamic element to the otherwise still environment. In the background, there is a building with illuminated signage, possibly a gas station or a similar establishment, which stands out against the dark sky. The overall atmosphere is quiet and somewhat isolated, with no visible pedestrians or significant activity aside from the moving vehicles. The camera remains fixed throughout the sequence, focusing on capturing the interplay between light and movement in this nocturnal urban setting.

caption: The video captures a dark, wet nighttime road viewed from a fixed camera, where moving lights dominate over resolved vehicles. A row of orange streetlights recedes into the distance on the left, and oncoming headlights form white starburst points with long vertical reflections on the slick pavement, the clusters holding position with minor flicker. On the right stands a low building bearing a small neon sign and a horizontal strip of lit panels, under bright overhead lamps. Two bright white horizontal streaks, one above the other, travel steadily rightward along the road, shrinking to a fragment at the edge before disappearing. A red light trail in the center likewise slides rightward across the clip, shifting from the middle toward the right-center and still visible in the last frame. A darker vehicle silhouette carrying red taillights on the right-center shows only a slight positional drift. The background streetlights and signage remain fixed throughout, confirming the camera is stationary.

an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
